articleTitle: Strowger and the invention of the automatic telephone exchange, 1879-1912
publicationTitle: IEE Discussion Meeting on Milestones in Telecommunications' and Lecture on 'The Life and Works of A H Reeves
abstract: In 1889, Strowger of Kansas City, USA, devised an automatic means of communication between two subscribers. The automatic telephone system was first introduced to the UK in 1897. This system provided for each subscriber's line to terminate on a two-motion switch and a multiple of subscribers' lines appeared in front of each switch mechanism. In 1899 a Strowger exhibit embodied the principle of trunking and grouping used in all subsequent installations. This paved the way towards systems of virtually unlimited capacity and was introduced simultaneously in France and Germany.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The introduction of digital switching in the 1960s
publicationTitle: IEE Discussion Meeting on Milestones in Telecommunications' and Lecture on 'The Life and Works of A H Reeves
abstract: The Empress digital tandem exchange was designed and constructed in the UK Post Office (PO) Research Laboratories, it was experimental and had limited objectives. Basically, it was to demonstrate that digital switching, involving time slot changing was a practical proposition using the technology which was then available. It was also designed to show that the high speed low energy technology could be operated in close proximity to Strowger equipment without suffering interference from the electric and magnetic fields and finally to determine whether the exchange could be maintained by staff normally involved with electro-mechanical equipment. Considerable testing was carried out in the laboratory to settle the question of interference and the exchange was finally installed in the apparatus room of a Strowger exchange.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The early years in the UK telephone service environment
publicationTitle: IEE Discussion Meeting on Milestones in Telecommunications' and Lecture on 'The Life and Works of A H Reeves
abstract: The first public manual exchange was brought into service at Coleman Street, London, in 1879 by the Telephone Company Ltd. The UK's first public service automatic telephone exchange, a Strowger system exchange manufactured by the Automatic Telephone Manufacturing Company of Liverpool, was opened at Epsom, Surrey, in 1912. This foreshadowed the conversion of the UK telephone network to automatic working and thus was a significant milestone. The basic Strowger system was not suitable for multi-exchange area application and an alternative approach was required. This was referred to as 'The Big City Problem'. The solution required translation of the exchange code digits to give routing flexibility over the local network. This gave rise to the register-translator concept; the beginning of the common control switching technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
